investor_summary:
## Key Drivers

• **ICICI Bank and other Indian financials** — Rising FCNR(B) deposit costs threatened bank margins and a Jefferies note flagged the risk of foreign investors reducing their allocation to Indian financials. With ICICI Bank a large fund holding, this sector-wide pressure was a key reason the fund declined.

• **InterGlobe Aviation (IndiGo)** — Retail inflation hit a 20-month high, raising concerns about continued RBI tightening and its effect on fuel and borrowing costs for airlines. The stock fell sharply over the week, dragging on fund performance.

• **State Bank of India** — A nationwide bank strike disrupted public-sector bank operations, while SBI's role in a large debt financing to Vodafone Idea raised credit-risk concerns. These negative developments weighed on the stock.

• **HDFC Bank and Axis Bank** — HDFC Bank's board shortlisted CEO candidates and sent names to the RBI, resolving a key uncertainty and prompting a bullish view from Macquarie. Jefferies also highlighted potential foreign investor reallocation toward Indian financials, and Moody's projected stronger deposit growth for banks, supporting both HDFC Bank and Axis Bank.

• **HCL Technologies** — A sharp rebound in IT stocks lifted HCL Tech, which gained up to 7% in a single session, providing a positive offset for the fund.

## Overall Summary

The fund ended the week lower, mainly because weakness in large financial holdings like ICICI Bank and State Bank of India, along with a sharp drop in InterGlobe Aviation, outweighed positive contributions. The financial sector faced concerns over rising FCNR(B) deposit costs and potential foreign investor outflows, while higher inflation pressured aviation. These drags were partly offset by strength in HDFC Bank, Axis Bank, and HCL Technologies, which benefited from improved sentiment around bank leadership, sector outlook, and an IT rebound. The net result was a weekly decline.
